factors.name: AIDataCenterTestBreadth
factors.basis: Teradyne launched UltraFLEXplus instruments on 2026-09-01 for high-power AI/data-center compute devices and introduced Iris 100 on 2026-09-21 for production microLED wafer/final test, extending current product evidence beyond the packet's July earnings sources.

risks: Product launches demonstrate capability and addressable use cases, not customer adoption, market share, realized revenue or pricing power.
unknowns: No unit shipments, customer names, bookings, product-specific revenue or margins were disclosed in these releases.
Alpha retains numeric underwriting and factor calibration authority.

factors.name: ProductRoadmapExecution
factors.basis: Two September product releases provide dated evidence that Teradyne is shipping/introducing test capability into AI/data-center and photonics-adjacent device roadmaps after the packet's July quarter.

risks: Roadmap execution can precede meaningful commercial conversion; launch cadence should not be treated as earnings evidence.
unknowns: Commercial ramp timing and contribution remain undisclosed.

observedFacts: Teradyne launched advanced UltraFLEXplus instruments engineered for AI and data-center computing devices.
The instruments target larger, higher-power compute devices and advanced packaging roadmaps.
Teradyne introduced Iris 100 for microLED wafer and final test.
The company states the system has a roadmap to support photodetector test capabilities in the same insertion.

recommendation: Reuse as current source-addressed product/catalyst and execution evidence while preserving absent commercial economics as unknown.
